questions.q: Match each delivery guarantee to how a consumer that writes its results to Kafka achieves it.
pairs: Save the position, then process the records
Process the records, then save the position
Write the output and the offsets in one transaction
questions.explain: The design docs split the semantics by when the position is saved. Saving it first loses records on a crash (at most once); saving it after processing may process them again (at least once, the default). Kafka-to-Kafka exactly once stores the consumer's position as a message in an internal topic and commits it in the same transaction as the output.

questions.q: A consume-transform-produce application's transaction is aborted. Put what happens next in order, first to last.
items: The offsets written in that transaction are discarded, so the stored position reverts
The application resets its consumer to the last committed position
The records are processed again, in a new transaction
questions.explain: On an abort the stored position reverts, but the consumer doesn't rewind by itself: the docs say the application must reset its consumer position. The simplest recovery is to recreate producer and consumer, which rewinds to the last committed offset.
